name: Adrian Vellum
role: Executive Director of the Meridian Museum
preparty_markdown:
Polished, ambitious, and almost unnervingly composed, Adrian has spent the last six years turning the

Meridian from a respected regional institution into a museum that expects to be mentioned in the same

sentence as the Met. He can greet a donor, calm a curator, and redirect a disaster without changing facial

expression. Tonight is his biggest gala yet, and he intends for it to look effortless.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Diplomatic under pressure; image-conscious; dryly funny; allergic to public chaos. Play him as someone who is always

hosting, even when he is not technically the host.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Works closely with Celeste Frame, though the two disagree about how much spectacle a museum should tolerate.

• Relies on Margot Ledger for the numbers and Helena Cross for donor agreements.

• Beatrice Plinth hired Adrian years ago and still occasionally speaks to him as if he were an intern.

COSTUME

Black tie or an immaculate dark suit; museum-lanyard-level precision without actually wearing a lanyard. Optional pocket

square, tasteful lapel pin, slim folder or program.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“A museum is just controlled chaos with better lighting.”

“Please do not use the phrase 'brand activation' within ten feet of a Rembrandt.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

Sterling had privately informed you that tonight's gift would come with a new governance agreement: he wanted veto power

over acquisitions, his name on the museum, and your resignation within sixty days. You smiled through the meeting and told

no one.

What you are hiding

You have already accepted a confidential offer to lead a rival museum next year, which makes any argument with Sterling

look like succession planning.

Do not volunteer this immediately. In Act II, protect it unless interrogation forces your hand; in Act III, reveal it if you need to defend yourself.

Your objectives

• Find out whether Margot has seen the governance addendum.

• Quietly learn whether Celeste would stay if you left.

• Do not volunteer your job offer unless pressure forces it.

• Sterling personally ordered Everett to take the Donor Salon camera offline for private meetings.

• Sterling threatened to withhold Lucian Gable's final design payment unless he accepted a last-minute display change.

name: Celeste Frame
preparty_markdown:
Celeste is the intellectual engine behind Treasures of the World: brilliant, exacting, and visibly pained by

sloppy labels, bad lighting, and people who call every old object an 'artifact.' She has spent years building the

Meridian's scholarly reputation and knows the exhibition better than anyone alive. She is gracious when she

chooses to be and devastating when she edits.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Controlled, observant, skeptical, quietly competitive. You do not need to be loud; a raised eyebrow can do half the work.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Professional counterpart to Adrian Vellum; they respect each other and routinely disagree.

• Mentors Sebastian Reed, the museum's graduate fellow.

• Frequently consults Rafael Gilt and Dr. Marcus Pryce on difficult objects.

COSTUME

Elegant gallery-black with one distinctive art-history touch: sculptural jewelry, silk scarf, statement earrings, or beautifully

severe glasses. Carry a pencil and small notebook.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“It is not 'mysterious.' It is mislabeled.”

“If anyone touches the glass, I will become part of the exhibition.”

What you are hiding

• Learn who wrote the anonymous warning note.

• Keep your independent report secret until you decide whom to trust.

• Marcus believes Sterling has suppressed provenance research connected to at least two Voss objects.
